row: My actual practice and development of massage techniques started long before I received formal training at MTIC through my association with a Tai Chi teacher who is trained in Asian massage arts. In 2003 he saved both of my knees from knee replacement surgeries by using Tui Na and other modalities. Since my knees grew stronger than ever, and the doctors were obviously wrong, this teacher became my mentor in Tai Chi and Qi Gong as well as my first massage therapist. I eventually learned to incorporate Tui Na and other techniques into my own massage routines, but today my most popular routines are chair massages which include PNF Tech Therapy. These routines are especially helpful to office workers who suffer from tight rhomboids, head-forward postures, and other symptoms of "office worker syndrome." PNF Tech Therapy is based on the Kaya Kalp healing system as it was practiced in Tibet many centuries ago, and I practice those techniques with an open heart and love for all life.
